question: Which mirror is used for shaving purpose?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Concave**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A concave mirror is used for shaving because it produces a magnified and erect image of the face, which makes it easier to shave:
 
• How it works
 
• When the face is placed close to the mirror, within its focus, the mirror produces a magnified and erect image
 
• Image type
 
• Produces images that are both genuine and reversed
 
• Other uses
 
• Also used for applying makeup
 
• Concave mirrors are curved, and as light hits the upper and lower portions of the mirror, the image is focused at a central point.
 
• The image changes depending on the distance between the item and the mirror. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Opaque**:

 
 
• **Opaque** materials do not allow light to pass through them.

 
 
• They block light completely, meaning you cannot see through opaque objects.
 
• Examples include wood, metal, and stone. In contrast to transparent or translucent materials, opaque materials prevent visibility through them.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Transparent**:
 
 
• **Transparent** materials allow light to pass through them completely, making objects behind them clearly visible.
 
• Glass, water, and clear plastic are examples of transparent materials.
 
• These materials enable us to see through them without distortion, as they allow most of the light to transmit.
 
 
 
• **Convex Mirror**:
 
 
• A **convex mirror** is a mirror that is curved outward, like the exterior of a sphere.
 
• Convex mirrors diverge light rays that strike them, meaning they spread out the reflected light.
 
• This property makes them useful in applications like car side mirrors and security mirrors, where a wide field of view is needed.
 
• Convex mirrors always produce virtual, upright, and diminished images.
